tags.gist: Agrees that variable outputs, third-party models, frequent changes and autonomous action make point-in-time premarket evaluation insufficient for some devices.
Wants FDA to distinguish initial authorization from continued reliance, which should depend on the original assumptions still holding.
Suggests higher-risk sponsors identify in advance their key assumptions, evidence, dependencies, thresholds, monitoring owners, change triggers and required responses.
Says manufacturers on third-party models need a defined evidentiary standard for deciding whether continued reliance remains justified.
Supports independent third parties, especially where sponsors pick their own benchmarks, another company supplies the model, or postmarket evidence gates continued operation.
Wants agentic evaluation to ask whether the system had authorization for that specific action under the conditions present, not only whether it worked.
Finds the two axes appropriate and says evidence for continued reliance on action-taking systems should rise with both.
Supports periodic re-benchmarking, degradation monitoring and defined reassessment triggers.
Asks FDA to formalize that authorization sets an initial reliance boundary, not permanent reliance, and to say what change requires re-testing the evidence.
